task_description: You're trying to add a shadcn/ui component using the CLI but it fails saying it can't find components.json. What file must exist in your project root and how do you create it?
deprecated_pattern:
# Trying to add without initialization
npx shadcn-ui@latest add button
correct_pattern:
# First initialize the project
npx shadcn@latest init
# Then add components
npx shadcn@latest add button
reference_solution:
# 1. Run init to create components.json and configure the project:
npx shadcn@latest init

# 2. Follow the prompts to set up:
# - Which style (new-york recommended)
# - Which base color
# - CSS variables for theming

# 3. Now add components:
npx shadcn@latest add button
npx shadcn@latest add dialog
npx shadcn@latest add form
why_models_fail_this: Developers unfamiliar with shadcn/ui often try to add components before running init. Models generating setup instructions sometimes omit the init step or show the wrong CLI invocation (shadcn-ui instead of shadcn).

task_description: Your components.json has style set to 'default'. This style is deprecated. What should you use instead?
why_models_fail_this: The 'default' style was one of two initial styles in shadcn/ui and appears in early tutorials. New projects use 'new-york' exclusively. Models generating components.json produce the old 'default' style.

task_description: You're importing a Button from shadcn/ui directly as a package. shadcn/ui is not a package - components live in your project. Fix the import.
deprecated_pattern:
import { Button } from 'shadcn-ui';
import { Button } from '@shadcn/ui';
why_models_fail_this: Developers accustomed to component libraries like Material UI or Ant Design expect to import from a package name. shadcn/ui works differently - it copies source code into the project. Models produce package-style imports that don't work.

task_description: Your shadcn/ui component uses React.forwardRef. In the Tailwind v4/React 19 update, shadcn/ui removed forwardRef from all components. Update the component pattern.
why_models_fail_this: React.forwardRef was the standard pattern for ref-forwarding in all React component libraries for years, including all shadcn/ui components pre-2025. React 19 made refs available as plain props, and shadcn/ui updated all components. Models generate the old forwardRef pattern.

task_description: Your code types a ref for a shadcn/ui component using React.ElementRef<typeof ComponentName>. With the removal of forwardRef in React 19 components, the typing approach changed. Update the ref type.
why_models_fail_this: React.ElementRef<typeof Component> was the standard way to type refs to shadcn/ui components when they used forwardRef. After React 19 and the forwardRef removal, you reference the underlying HTML element type directly. Models produce the old ElementRef pattern.

task_description: You're setting up a new project with Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui. Your tailwind.config.js file is empty because Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration. What should the tailwind.config value be in components.json?
why_models_fail_this: In Tailwind CSS v3, a tailwind.config.js file was always required and its path was configured in components.json. Tailwind v4 moved to CSS-first configuration, so there's no JS config file. Models generate tailwind.config pointing to a config file that doesn't exist.

task_description: After migrating to Tailwind CSS v4, your shadcn/ui chart component references colors as hsl(var(--chart-1)). With the Tailwind v4 @theme inline pattern, the CSS variables already wrap the hsl values. Update the chart config.
why_models_fail_this: With Tailwind v3, shadcn/ui CSS variables stored raw HSL values (e.g., --chart-1: 12 76% 61%) requiring hsl() wrapper in usage. With Tailwind v4's @theme inline pattern, the hsl() is baked into the variable value, so double-wrapping breaks the color. Models trained on v3 patterns produce the old hsl(var(--chart-1)) form.

task_description: Your project uses the tailwindcss-animate plugin for shadcn/ui animations. This plugin was deprecated in March 2025. What should you use instead?
reference_solution:
# 1. Remove old plugin
npm uninstall tailwindcss-animate

# 2. Install replacement
npm install -D tw-animate-css

# globals.css - replace @plugin with @import
# Before:
# @plugin 'tailwindcss-animate';

# After:
@import "tw-animate-css";

# For Tailwind v3 projects that use tailwind.config.js:
# Before: plugins: [require('tailwindcss-animate')]
# After: import 'tw-animate-css' in your CSS
why_models_fail_this: tailwindcss-animate was the animation library installed with all shadcn/ui setups for years and appears in every setup guide. The switch to tw-animate-css is a breaking configuration change that models trained before 2025 will not know about.

task_description: You're using the toast component from shadcn/ui to show notifications. This component is being deprecated in favor of Sonner. Show how to use Sonner as the replacement.
why_models_fail_this: The toast component with useToast hook was the recommended notification pattern in shadcn/ui for years. Its deprecation in favor of Sonner means all models trained on earlier guides produce the old useToast pattern.

task_description: Your shadcn/ui Button component used to show a pointer cursor on hover. The default was changed to the default cursor. If you want pointer cursor back, how do you add it?
deprecated_pattern: // Old default: cursor-pointer was included in Button by default
correct_pattern:
<Button className="cursor-pointer">Click me</Button>
// Or globally in components.json/tailwind override
why_models_fail_this: cursor-pointer was included in the Button component for its entire history until the 2025 Tailwind v4 update. Models trained before this change will generate Button components with cursor-pointer included by default, or will not know it needs to be explicitly added.

task_description: You're building a custom component that extends shadcn/ui styles and want to merge className props safely with conditional classes. What utility do shadcn/ui components use for this, and where does it come from?
why_models_fail_this: Template literal className merging silently drops conflicting Tailwind classes (the last rule wins in CSS but template literals can't override). shadcn/ui's cn() utility from @/lib/utils properly deduplicates conflicting Tailwind classes using tailwind-merge. Models use template literals instead.

task_description: You're running the shadcn/ui CLI using the old package name from tutorials. The CLI package was renamed. Fix the init command.
deprecated_pattern:
npx shadcn-ui@latest init
npx shadcn-ui@latest add button
correct_pattern:
npx shadcn@latest init
npx shadcn@latest add button
reference_solution:
# The CLI package was renamed from shadcn-ui to shadcn

# Initialize a new project:
npx shadcn@latest init

# Add components:
npx shadcn@latest add button
npx shadcn@latest add card dialog form input label

# Or with pnpm:
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add button
why_models_fail_this: The CLI was originally published as shadcn-ui and every tutorial from 2023 shows npx shadcn-ui@latest. The rename to shadcn in 2024 means the old command fails with package not found. This is one of the most common errors developers encounter.

task_description: You have a form inside a Dialog and want to close the dialog programmatically after form submission. Show the correct pattern using shadcn/ui's Dialog component.
deprecated_pattern:
// Wrong: trying to close by toggling show state without the component's own state
<Dialog>
  <DialogContent>
    <form onSubmit={() => setShowDialog(false)}>
      ...
    </form>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
correct_pattern:
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogContent>
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}> // handleSubmit calls setOpen(false)
      ...
    </form>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
why_models_fail_this: Controlled dialogs with open and onOpenChange is the Radix pattern but many developers miss it. Models often generate uncontrolled dialogs or use incorrect methods to close dialogs programmatically after async operations.

task_description: You're building a form with shadcn/ui. The correct pattern uses the Form components with React Hook Form. Show the minimal correct setup for a controlled form field with validation.
deprecated_pattern:
// Wrong: using input directly without Form wrapper
<Input name="email" onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
why_models_fail_this: The shadcn/ui Form component wraps React Hook Form with specific form-related sub-components (FormField, FormItem, FormControl, FormMessage). Models unfamiliar with this pattern use raw inputs with useState, missing the accessibility features and validation wiring.

task_description: After upgrading shadcn/ui components for React 19, every primitive now has a data-slot attribute. How do you use data-slot for styling a specific part of a complex component?
deprecated_pattern:
/* Old approach: use displayName-based selectors or deeply nested CSS */
.my-accordion .AccordionItem { border-bottom: 2px solid red; }
correct_pattern:
/* Use data-slot for targeting component parts */
[data-slot='accordion-item'] { border-bottom: 2px solid red; }
why_models_fail_this: The data-slot attribute system is new in the React 19 component update for shadcn/ui. Models trained before this change don't know about data-slot and use older styling approaches (CSS class selectors, nested component targeting) that are less reliable.
